To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
paid work, not living with their partners, and fewer childcare consultations were associated with inadequate feeding practices.
the practices of the mothers/caregivers in relation to the diet of children were inadequate due to the few accomplished steps.

paid maternal work outside the house, not living with partner, performing less than seven consultations, and the number of meals per day were associated with inadequate feeding practices in the studied population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the practices of the mothers/caregivers regarding the diet of their children under 1 year of age, in accordance with the recommendations of the Ten Steps for Healthy Feeding.
the importance of the ten steps to promote healthy feeding in children under one year old, and to contribute to a reduction in infant morbidity and mortality.
the implementation of the ten steps of breastfeeding in the context of the family and the health service.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the practices of mothers/caregivers regarding the diet of their children under 12 months of age were considered inadequate due mainly to the low compliance of the ten steps of healthy feeding.

the practices of the mothers/caregivers in relation to the children's diet are inadequate due to the small number of steps achieved, and the determinants are paid maternal work outside the household, not living with a partner and performing less child healthcare consultations.

the practices of mothers or caregivers of the study population in relation to the diet of children between 12-23months and 29 days old are considered inadequate due to low compliance with the number of accomplished ten steps.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ten steps for the healthy feeding of children are not yet well known by the population, and this fact may be related to the low number of childcare consultations.
there is a need for a more comprehensive and integrated health care model for mothers and caregivers in order to promote the healthy development of infants.
there is a need to develop and implement actions that encourage the practice of healthy feeding among mothers and caregivers of children under one-year of age.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is necessary to develop actions that promote breastfeeding and adequate complementary feeding in the first year of life, especially for mothers who work outside the home and who do not live with their partners.

health professionals should pay attention to the social context of families, especially the employment of the mother, to identify the needs for the implementation of actions to improve the practices of feeding children under one year.
the health care team needs to strengthen the promotion and health education of the mothers and their caregivers regarding the diet and feeding practices of children under one.
